taskTitle: Twelve HTTP status codes, by the book

checks.detail: 1 phase had the tools designed for them

finalText:
Every section I needed is in RFC 9110 (the current HTTP Semantics spec), which I've now read. Here are the results.

I used RFC 9110, "HTTP Semantics", at https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html. It obsoletes RFC 7231. Each status code is defined in Section 15 of that document.

**Heuristically cacheable (the spec says so in the code's own section):** 203, 206, 308, 405, 410, 414 and 501.

**Not heuristically cacheable (the spec makes no such statement for these):** 303, 307, 413, 421 and 422. Section 15 does not call any of them heuristically cacheable, so I marked them false. The RFC 9111 caching spec has its own heuristic-caching rules. I did not open it, so this rests on RFC 9110 alone.

**Reason phrases that changed from RFC 7231:** 413 is now "Content Too Large" (it was "Payload Too Large"). 422 is "Unprocessable Content" (it was "Unprocessable Entity").

The page's text wraps lines. I joined the quoted sentences onto single lines.
